LB Dre Greenlaw (neck) is Questionable [ic3] and has averaged 76.0% of snaps [ic4] over 8 games [ic5], so his absence would thin linebacker depth. RB Jordan James (calf) is also Questionable [ic6], but he carries only 3.9% of team rushes [ic7] over 254 team rushes [ic8], so the ground game barely shifts if he sits. Seattle's latest report has QB Sam Darnold (ribs) as Out [ic10] and OT Charles Cross (ankle) as Out [ic11]. Darnold's absence would concentrate passing volume on J.Smith-Njigba, who takes 37.1% of team targets [ic12] over 294 team targets [ic13].

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Third down decides this game. SF passes on 72.9% of third downs [mc1] over 107 plays [mc2] and converts 52.3% [mc3], while its defense allows 42.1% conversions [mc4] over 133 plays [mc5], 20th in the league [mc6]. Seattle's defense produces a 20.2% pressure proxy [mc7] over 357 dropbacks [mc8], but SF blitzes on 28.9% of dropbacks [mc9], so keep throws quick. Second, the run fits: SF's defense averages 6.6 defenders in the box on runs [mc10] over 222 run plays [mc11]. Eric Wilson takes 41.0% of Seattle's rushes [mc12], and Dre Greenlaw, listed Questionable, has played 76.0% of snaps [mc13]; if he sits, the middle of SF's run fits thins. Third, the red zone: SF has scored on 85.3% of red-zone drives [mc14] over 34 drives [mc15], and its defense allows a 51.6% TD rate [mc16] over 31 drives [mc17]. McCaffrey takes 50.0% of designed carries [mc18], so the goal-line plan runs through him. Fourth, Pineiro is 40.0% from 50-plus [mc21] on 5 attempts [mc22], so treat long kicks as a low-confidence option.
